title: Christoffel symbols of the round sphere
promptMarkdown:
On the chart $W$ of the sphere $S^2_R$ from unit 1, with $x^1=\theta$, $x^2=\varphi$ and $g=R^2\,d\theta^2+R^2\sin^2\theta\,d\varphi^2$, state your index conventions and then:

1. Write down $(g^{ij})$.
2. Compute all eight Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^k_{ij}$ of the Levi-Civita connection from the formula $\Gamma^k_{ij}=\tfrac12g^{kl}(\partial_ig_{jl}+\partial_jg_{il}-\partial_lg_{ij})$, showing the work for every non-zero symbol and saying why the others vanish.
3. Verify the torsion-free symmetry $\Gamma^k_{ij}=\Gamma^k_{ji}$ in your table, and verify one instance of metric compatibility directly: check that $\partial_\theta g_{\varphi\varphi}=2\,g(\nabla_{\partial_\theta}\partial_\varphi,\partial_\varphi)$ using your symbols.
4. One of your symbols is unbounded as $\theta\to0$. Explain why this does not mean that the Levi-Civita connection of $S^2_R$ is singular at the north pole; give a reason that does not rely on computing in another chart.
5. Observe that $R$ does not appear in your table, and prove in general that the Levi-Civita connections of $g$ and of $c\,g$ ($c>0$ constant) coincide.
hintLadder: Only one metric coefficient has a non-zero derivative, and it depends on $\theta$ alone. Which terms of the formula can therefore survive?
Since $(g_{ij})$ is diagonal, so is $(g^{ij})$, and the formula for $\Gamma^k_{ij}$ has a single term in the sum over $l$, namely $l=k$.
For part 4, recall Theorem 6.20: what is the Levi-Civita connection of a submanifold of Euclidean space, and is that description smooth at the pole?
For part 5, write the Koszul formula for $c\,g$ and factor out $c$ from both sides, or scale $g^{kl}$ and $\partial_ig_{jl}$ in the Christoffel formula.

checkExamples.label: correct LaTeX table
checkExamples.text: Conventions: $\nabla_{\partial_i}\partial_j=\Gamma^k_{ij}\partial_k$. With $g^{\theta\theta}=R^{-2}$, $g^{\varphi\varphi}=(R^2\sin^2\theta)^{-1}$ and $\partial_\theta g_{\varphi\varphi}=2R^2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ the only non-zero symbols are $\Gamma^\theta_{\varphi\varphi}=-\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and $\Gamma^\varphi_{\theta\varphi}=\Gamma^\varphi_{\varphi\theta}=\cot\theta$. Check: $2g(\nabla_{\partial_\theta}\partial_\varphi,\partial_\varphi)=2\cot\theta\cdot R^2\sin^2\theta=2R^2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\partial_\theta g_{\varphi\varphi}$. The Christoffel symbols are not tensor components, so the blow-up of $\cot\theta$ at the pole is a coordinate artefact; the connection is the tangential projection of the Euclidean derivative and is smooth.

checkExamples.label: plain-text with cos/sin
checkExamples.text: Gamma^phi_{theta phi} = cos θ / sin θ and Gamma^theta_{phi phi} = -cos θ sin θ; all other symbols are zero because the only varying coefficient is g_φφ.

checkExamples.label: tensor claim
checkExamples.text: Since the Christoffel symbols are the components of a tensor, their blow-up at the poles shows the connection is singular there.

checkExamples.label: missing symbols
checkExamples.text: All Christoffel symbols vanish because the metric is diagonal.
